parsed.why: Most-protective tier state: no facility ban, 1993 gender-identity anti-discrimination and hate-crime coverage, shield law covering travelling families, open markers, X licences, care coverage. Only national passport/entry regime caps it.

Tier-1 universal exposure: criminalised bathroom use extending to private businesses, up to a year jail, in force July 2026 with no demonstrated remedy; plus birth-certificate ban, athletics ban, pronoun and minor-disclosure rules. Below parent.

Birth-sex facility endorsement by executive order, surgery-only markers, under-19 care ban, athletics ban, no state GI hate-crime or discrimination law, and documented birth-sex custody placement with sexual assault plus court dismissal — hostile layer under parent.

No facility ban, 2013 gender-identity anti-discrimination with penalties for GI-motivated violence, easy marker change, low-risk national classification, LGBTQ commission. Protections are relative rather than specialised, but no documented visitor-facing hostility beyond the parent regime.

2020 civil-rights and hate-crime statutes, panic-defence repeal, X markers, accessible birth certificates — offset by official hostility: school bathroom/pronoun bans, athletics exclusion, court upholding misgendering, vetoed GI bullying definition.
